feature: Zoom regions that frame a spot and can follow the pointer
summary: A recording can zoom in on one spot for a while: a bar under the clip says when, a box on the picture says where, and the box can ride along with the recorded pointer. Suggest Zooms puts one round every run of clicks.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open a recording made by Photonz (it keeps where the pointer went); an older recording works too, without Follow Cursor.

try.do: Put the playhead where something happens, right-click the clip, choose Add Zoom.
With the zoom picked, drag the box on the picture to move it, or pull a corner to go in more or less.
On the Zoom lane under the clip, drag the bar's ends, or the small marks inside it to make the way in and out longer.
Right-click the zoom's bar and choose Follow Cursor, then scrub: the box rides the pointer.
Scrub across the zoom with it picked and watch the box follow.
Click beside the box to let the zoom go, then play: the picture zooms in, follows and eases back out.
On a recording with clicks, right-click the clip and choose Suggest Zooms.

evaluate: Is showing the whole picture with the box while a zoom is picked the right way to frame it, or do you want to see the zoomed result while you adjust?
Does a following zoom glide the way you want, or is it too lazy or too twitchy?
Is the Zoom lane under the clip where you would look for zooms?
Is Add Zoom on the clip's right-click (and the ruler's, and the Clip menu) enough, or do you want a key for it?
Are 0.7 second eases and 200% good defaults for a new zoom?
rough: No mock draws a zoom region (video-zoom-wt is the punch-in, which still ships). This follows Screen Studio's shape: a bar for when, a box for where.
While framing, the clip's own selection handles show round the whole picture as well as the zoom's box, so there are two boxes on screen.
The pointer does not change over the box's corners or body yet, so nothing says a corner can be pulled until you try it.
Escape does not let go of a picked zoom; a click beside the box, on the empty lane, or on another clip does.
Follow Cursor reads the pointer against the whole recording, so on a clip that has been cropped the box follows a little off.
The render change was not timed on its own: it uses the same enlarging resampler as Punch In, which measured 10 ms for a 12 megapixel frame at 200%.
